experiment_description: Central concept: test whether Λ-enhanced gray molasses (ΛGM), which combines velocity-selective coherent population trapping with blue-detuned polarization-gradient cooling in a Λ system, can increase loading of an unusually shallow nanophotonic cesium-atom trap compared with conventional red-detuned polarization-gradient cooling (RPGC). The apparatus uses laser-cooled Cs atoms near the evanescent field of a tapered optical nanofiber with nominal waist radius 225 nm. The two-color nanofiber trap uses a fiber-guided red-detuned standing wave at wavelength 935 nm launched from both fiber ends with 55 µW total setting per paper convention, and a fiber-guided blue-detuned running wave at wavelength 685 nm with 7.75 mW; the calculated trap minimum is about 270 nm from the nanofiber surface and the calculated trap depth is 24 µK. A 3D MOT prepares the cloud for 1.5 s using a D2 cooler red-detuned by 2 natural linewidths ΓD2 from the Cs F=4 to F′=5 transition and a D2 repumper resonant with F=3 to F′=4, with counter-propagating σ+ and σ− beams. During a 19 ms transition phase the magnetic-field gradient is ramped to zero, D2 cooling intensity is reduced, and D2 detuning is increased to 11 ΓD2. The loading sequence then applies RPGC on the D2 line for variable durations up to about 50 ms and then switches to ΛGM on the D1 line for variable durations up to about 200 ms. In ΛGM, two phase-coherent light fields couple the two Cs hyperfine ground states to the 6P1/2, F′=4 state; the D1 cooler is blue-detuned from F=4 to F′=4 by Δ1P=4.5 ΓD1, and the second phase-coherent field is generated with an electro-optic modulator near the Cs ground-state hyperfine splitting with a sideband-to-carrier ratio of 1:4. The two-photon detuning is held at the experimentally selected near-resonant value for the loading-time measurement. The spatial scope is the nanofiber-guided dipole trap along the fiber waist, consisting of two diametral one-dimensional arrays of trapping sites with axial period λred/(2 neff), where neff=1.08. For each loading time, the dependent variable is obtained by weak fiber-guided transmission spectroscopy on the D2 F=4 to F′=5 transition; the probe is scanned for 500 µs at approximately 10^-2 times the saturation power, with transverse probe polarization parallel to the plane containing the trapped atoms, and the optical depth is extracted by fitting the transmission spectrum with a saturated Lorentzian.

rpgc_asymptotic_optical_depth.description: The fitted steady-state optical depth reached when loading the nanofiber trap using the RPGC stage alone under the specified sequence.

rpgc_asymptotic_optical_depth_uncertaint.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the fitted RPGC steady-state optical depth.

rpgc_loading_time_constant_ms.description: The exponential loading time constant obtained from the RPGC optical-depth-versus-time data.

rpgc_loading_time_constant_uncertainty_m.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the RPGC exponential loading time constant.

lambda_gm_asymptotic_optical_depth.description: The fitted steady-state optical depth reached after switching from the RPGC stage to the ΛGM loading stage under the specified sequence.

lambda_gm_asymptotic_optical_depth_uncer.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the fitted ΛGM steady-state optical depth.

lambda_gm_loading_time_constant_ms.description: The exponential loading time constant obtained from the ΛGM optical-depth-versus-time data.

lambda_gm_loading_time_constant_uncertai.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the ΛGM exponential loading time constant.

lambda_gm_od_enhancement_over_rpgc.description: The ratio of the steady-state optical depth after ΛGM loading to that after RPGC-only loading in the same nanofiber trap.

experiment_description: Central concept: characterize the cooling action of the ΛGM stage used to load a nanophotonic Cs trap by measuring the temperature of the surrounding untrapped molasses cloud, because lower temperature is expected to increase capture into the very small trap volumes near the optical nanofiber. A Cs MOT is prepared with the D2 cooler and repumper beams as in the nanofiber experiment, followed by the 19 ms magnetic-field and D2-cooling transition ramp and a 45 ms RPGC stage on the D2 transition. ΛGM is then applied on the D1 transition using counter-propagating σ+ and σ− beams coupling the Cs F=3 and F=4 ground states to 6P1/2, F′=4; the D1 cooler is detuned by Δ1P=4.5 ΓD1 from F=4 to F′=4, the second phase-coherent field is generated by an EOM near the hyperfine splitting, and the two-photon detuning Δ2P is either swept across the near-resonance range shown in the paper or set at zero for the duration-dependent measurement. The temperature measurement applies to the untrapped free-space Cs atom cloud in the vicinity of the nanofiber rather than to atoms already bound in the evanescent-field trap. The cloud temperature is measured by time-of-flight imaging after releasing the atoms, with ΛGM durations including a short fixed-duration detuning scan and a duration scan extending to the long-cooling condition used to characterize the final ΛGM temperature.

rpgc_cloud_temperature_uK.description: The time-of-flight temperature of the untrapped Cs cloud after the RPGC stage before applying ΛGM.

rpgc_cloud_temperature_uncertainty_uK.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the RPGC cloud temperature.

lambda_gm_cloud_temperature_after_long_c.description: The time-of-flight temperature of the untrapped Cs cloud after the long-duration ΛGM cooling condition.
The one-standard-error uncertainty of the long-duration ΛGM cloud temperature.

experiment_description: Central concept: determine the two-photon detuning condition under which ΛGM most effectively loads atoms into the nanofiber trap, testing the role of the velocity-selective dark state in the small-volume nanophotonic capture process. The same Cs nanofiber trap is used: a 225 nm nominal-radius nanofiber waist, 935 nm red-detuned standing-wave trap field at 55 µW launched from both directions, 685 nm blue-detuned running-wave trap field at 7.75 mW, calculated trap depth 24 µK, and trap sites at two diametral arrays near the nanofiber surface. The atoms are first prepared in the MOT and RPGC sequence, then ΛGM is applied on the D1 line with Δ1P=4.5 ΓD1 and a phase-coherent second field generated by an EOM with sideband-to-carrier ratio 1:4. The independent variable is the ΛGM two-photon detuning Δ2P, scanned over the approximately ±100 kHz range around the hyperfine two-photon resonance. For each detuning, the final nanofiber-trapped optical depth is obtained by fiber-guided weak-probe transmission spectroscopy on the D2 F=4 to F′=5 transition and normalized to the maximum optical depth within the scan; the detuning dependence is fit with a Gaussian to extract the peak position. The measurement samples the same guided-mode interaction region of the nanofiber trap and is sensitive to residual light shifts and magnetic fields through shifts of the optimum dark-state condition.

lambda_gm_optimal_two_photon_detuning_kH.description: The fitted two-photon detuning at which the ΛGM loading optical depth is maximal.

lambda_gm_optimal_two_photon_detuning_un.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the fitted optimum ΛGM two-photon detuning.

experiment_description: Central concept: independently quantify the number of atoms coupled to the nanofiber and the single-atom coupling probability after ΛGM-assisted loading, establishing whether the enhanced loading produces a large guided-mode optical depth in a shallow nanophotonic trap. The sample is a Cs ensemble loaded into the two-color nanofiber trap at the waist of a 225 nm nominal-radius tapered optical fiber, using the MOT, RPGC, and ΛGM sequence described for the loading experiment. The optical depth is measured by scanning a weak nanofiber-guided probe across the Cs D2 F=4 to F′=5 transition at approximately 10^-2 Psat for a 500 µs scan; the probe polarization is transverse and parallel to the plane containing the trapped atoms, and the transmission spectrum is fit with a saturated Lorentzian. The atom number is measured in the same class of loaded ensembles by a depumping method: a weak 1.3 pW nanofiber-guided probe resonant with the Cs D2 F=4 to F′=4 transition, with transverse polarization orthogonal to the plane containing the trapped atoms, is sent as a boxcar-shaped pulse through the fiber; the time-dependent transmission is fit to the optical-pumping model of Ref. [49], equivalently checked by counting missing photons while accounting for branching ratios to the two hyperfine ground states. The guided-mode emission probability is then derived as β=OD/(4N), where OD is the resonant optical depth of the trapped ensemble and N is the atom number. The spatial scope is the nanofiber-waist trap region addressed by the guided probe, integrating over the ensemble along the fiber rather than imaging individual sites.

representative_optical_depth.description: The optical depth extracted from a representative weak-probe transmission spectrum after ΛGM-assisted loading.

representative_optical_depth_uncertainty.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the representative optical-depth fit.

depumping_atom_number.description: The total number of nanofiber-trapped Cs atoms extracted from the depumping transmission dynamics.

depumping_atom_number_uncertainty.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the depumping-derived atom number.

single_atom_waveguide_decay_probability_.description: The guided-mode spontaneous-emission probability per excited atom derived from optical depth and atom number using β=OD/(4N).
The one-standard-error uncertainty of the derived guided-mode spontaneous-emission probability.

experiment_description: Central concept: determine whether ΛGM-assisted loading drives the nanofiber trap into the collisional blockade filling regime, where at most one Cs atom occupies each trap site and the expected site-occupation ceiling is set by light-assisted two-body loss. The nanofiber trap uses the same 935 nm red-detuned standing-wave and 685 nm blue-detuned running-wave fields, forming two diametral one-dimensional arrays of sites above and below the nanofiber. The site spacing used to convert line density to filling factor is λred/(2 neff)=935 nm/(2×1.08), and both diametral arrays are included in the filling calculation. To prepare a high-atom-number ensemble for imaging, the MOT is loaded for 1.2 s, followed by 60 ms of RPGC and 190 ms of ΛGM loading. The trapped ensemble is illuminated through the nanofiber using the D2 EIT-cooling light fields detuned by about 7.3 ΓD2, and fluorescence is imaged perpendicular to the guided-light propagation direction onto an Andor iXon Ultra EMCCD. The image in the analysis is accumulated by repeating the imaging sequence 3000 times with 23 ms integration/probing time per shot. The spatial analysis covers the fiber-waist region visible in the EMCCD image, including the approximately millimeter-scale central portion away from the up-taper where the evanescent trapping intensity decreases; the local line density from fluorescence is combined with an independent total atom-number measurement to infer the local filling factor along the nanofiber.

maximum_site_filling_factor.description: The maximum inferred probability for a single trap site in one of the two nanofiber arrays to be occupied by a Cs atom.

flat_top_distribution_length_mm.description: The length along the nanofiber over which the inferred atom distribution is approximately flat-topped near its maximum filling condition.

collisional_blockade_regime_reached.description: Whether the inferred filling behavior is consistent with operation at the single-atom-per-site collisional blockade limit.

experiment_description: Central concept: test whether applying the same free-space ΛGM light fields after loading can act as EIT-assisted cooling for atoms already bound in the shallow nanofiber trap, thereby extending trap storage without relying on reloading from the surrounding cloud. The Cs ensemble is first loaded into the 24 µK two-color nanofiber trap using the MOT, RPGC, and ΛGM loading sequence. After loading, all molasses beams are turned off and the optical depth is measured as a function of hold time in the trap to obtain the passive loss curve. For the active-cooling condition, all molasses beams remain off during an initial waiting time long enough for untrapped atoms in the surrounding cloud to fall below the nanofiber, then the ΛGM beams are turned on again after specified delays such as 45 ms or about 175–195 ms. The ΛGM fields use the D1 Λ system coupling the Cs hyperfine ground states to 6P1/2, F′=4 with the D1 cooler detuned by Δ1P=4.5 ΓD1 and the phase-coherent second field set near the two-photon resonance. The measurement probes only atoms remaining in the nanofiber-guided trap after the waiting interval and tracks the ensemble-integrated guided-mode optical depth by weak D2 F=4 to F′=5 transmission spectroscopy as a function of hold time over hundreds of milliseconds. Exponential fits to OD versus hold time define the passive and active storage time constants.

passive_storage_time_ms.description: The exponential decay time of the nanofiber-trapped atom optical depth with all molasses beams off after loading.

passive_storage_time_uncertainty_ms.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the passive storage time fit for the free-space ΛGM cooling comparison.

lambda_gm_active_storage_time_ms.description: The exponential decay time of the nanofiber-trapped atom optical depth when the ΛGM light fields are reapplied after the post-loading wait.

lambda_gm_active_storage_time_uncertaint.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the active storage time fit with ΛGM/EIT-assisted cooling.

lambda_gm_storage_time_enhancement_facto.description: The ratio of active storage time with the reapplied ΛGM light fields to the passive storage time in the same trap configuration.

experiment_description: Central concept: determine whether free-space ΛGM/EIT-assisted cooling preserves the atom–nanofiber coupling strength during storage by counteracting motional heating in the shallow evanescent-field trap. The same nanofiber-trapped Cs ensemble is prepared using the MOT, RPGC, and ΛGM loading sequence in the two-color trap with 935 nm standing-wave red field and 685 nm running-wave blue field. After loading, the atoms are either held passively with all molasses beams off or held with the D1 ΛGM fields reapplied after the waiting interval used to avoid loading from the falling untrapped cloud. At selected hold times normalized by the passive storage time τp, two independent guided-probe measurements are performed: resonant D2 F=4 to F′=5 transmission spectroscopy gives OD, and D2 F=4 to F′=4 depumping transmission gives atom number N. The coupling strength is calculated as β=OD/(4N), where β is the probability for an excited Cs atom to emit into the guided nanofiber mode. The measurement integrates over the full trapped ensemble addressed by the guided mode and compares the time dependence of β for passive and actively cooled storage conditions.

passive_beta_time_trend.description: The observed time dependence of the derived atom–waveguide coupling probability during passive storage.

lambda_gm_cooled_beta_time_trend.description: The observed time dependence of the derived atom–waveguide coupling probability during storage with reapplied ΛGM/EIT-assisted cooling.

lambda_gm_cooled_beta_percent.description: The approximate maintained atom–waveguide coupling probability during the actively cooled hold.

experiment_description: Central concept: demonstrate an all-guided-light implementation of EIT cooling in a nanophotonic trap, exploiting the radially decaying nanofiber evanescent field to address radial motional sidebands with co-propagating guided fields rather than external paraxial beams. Cs atoms are first loaded into the same shallow two-color nanofiber trap. After loading, a waiting interval is inserted so that untrapped atoms fall away from the nanofiber, and then two additional phase-coherent nanofiber-guided fields co-propagate through the fiber to establish a Λ system on the Cs D2 line via F′=4. The strong coupling field is blue-detuned from the F=4 to F′=4 transition by Δ1P,EIT,C=2.5 ΓD2 for the storage-time measurement, with guided power in the few-hundred-picowatt range; sidebands are generated by a fiber-based phase modulator with carrier-to-sideband ratio 13:1. The transverse polarization of the EIT-cooling fields is aligned orthogonal to the plane containing the trapped atoms. Passive and active storage curves are measured by recording the nanofiber-guided optical depth versus hold time after loading, with the active guided-EIT condition switched on after a 41 ms delay. The exponential decay of OD over the measured hold interval defines the passive and guided-EIT-cooled storage times for the same nanofiber trap geometry.

guided_eit_passive_storage_time_ms.description: The exponential optical-depth decay time for the nanofiber-trapped atoms without guided EIT cooling in the guided-light comparison measurement.

guided_eit_passive_storage_time_uncertai.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the passive storage time in the guided-EIT comparison measurement.

guided_eit_active_storage_time_ms.description: The exponential optical-depth decay time when co-propagating nanofiber-guided EIT-cooling fields are applied after the post-loading delay.

guided_eit_active_storage_time_uncertain.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the guided-EIT active storage time.

guided_eit_storage_time_enhancement_fact.description: The ratio of active storage time with guided EIT cooling to passive storage time in the same measurement sequence.

experiment_description: Central concept: identify the cooling resonance and motional frequency associated with the all-guided EIT-cooling mechanism in the nanofiber trap. The loaded Cs atoms are held in the same 24 µK two-color nanofiber-guided trap, and the EIT-cooling fields are two phase-coherent co-propagating D2 guided fields coupling the Cs hyperfine ground states through F′=4. For the two-photon detuning scan, the optical depth is measured after a fixed 20 ms guided-EIT cooling interval while the two-photon detuning Δ2P,EIT is scanned across the resonance; Δ2P,EIT is defined as zero when probe and coupling fields couple the two hyperfine ground states without changing motional quantum number. Negative Δ2P,EIT addresses sideband cooling and positive detuning addresses sideband heating. For the coupling-strength scan, the one-photon detuning Δ1P,EIT,C of the strong coupling field is set to values in the plotted MHz-scale range, the coupling Rabi frequency Ω1P,EIT,C is varied by changing the guided coupling-field power, and the optical depth after EIT cooling is used to locate the maximum. The EIT cooling condition used for comparison is (1/2)[sqrt(Δ1P,EIT,C^2+Ω1P,EIT,C^2)-|Δ1P,EIT,C|]=ν, where Δ1P,EIT,C is the one-photon detuning of the guided coupling field, Ω1P,EIT,C is its Rabi frequency, and ν is the relevant trap oscillation frequency inferred from fitting the optimum Rabi-frequency positions. The measurement samples the nanofiber-trapped ensemble addressed by the guided evanescent fields and is sensitive to radial, azimuthal, and axial motional contributions within the one-dimensional EIT-cooling model.

guided_eit_optimal_two_photon_detuning_k.description: The two-photon detuning at which the guided-EIT cooling scan gives the largest post-cooling optical depth.

guided_eit_optimal_coupler_power_pW.description: The guided coupling-field power at which the post-cooling optical depth is maximal for the specified one-photon detuning condition.

guided_eit_optimal_coupler_power_fractio.description: The coupling-field power at the optical-depth maximum expressed as a fraction of the saturation power.

guided_eit_fitted_trap_frequency_kHz.description: The trap oscillation frequency inferred by fitting the optimum guided-EIT coupling Rabi frequencies to the EIT-cooling resonance condition.

guided_eit_fitted_trap_frequency_uncerta.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the trap frequency inferred from the guided-EIT resonance fit.

experiment_description: Central concept: compare ΛGM and RPGC loading dynamics at the single-site rate-equation level to determine whether the enhanced ΛGM loading is limited by collisional blockade in the nanofiber trap. The nanofiber trap is the same two-color evanescent-field trap with two diametral arrays of sites and an estimated atom-cloud length along the nanofiber of 1.5 mm for counting available trapping sites. The number of available sites is determined using the axial period λred/(2 neff) with λred=935 nm and neff=1.08 and by including the two arrays. The atom number N(t) used for loading-rate extraction is inferred from the measured optical-depth loading curves via N=OD/(4β), using β=1% for this rate estimate. The one-atom loading rate R for each cooling method is obtained from the initial slope dN/dt at the onset of the RPGC or ΛGM loading stage divided by the number of available traps. The one-atom loss rate γ is obtained as γ=1/τ, where τ is the storage time of trapped atoms while applying the respective cooling method. For comparison with collisional blockade, the trap volume V is calculated from the full widths at half maximum of the trap potential in cylindrical coordinates, dr=270 nm, dθ=0.87 rad, dz=150 nm, and the relation V=dr dz dθ r ln[1/(1−η)] sqrt[η/(1−η)], where η=kBT/|U0|, T is the atom temperature, U0 is the trap depth, kB is Boltzmann’s constant, and r is the trap radius from the fiber axis; the Cs two-body loss coefficient κ=10×10^-10 cm^3 s^-1 is used to compute κ/(4V). The regime criterion is γ/2<R<κ/(4V) for collisional-blockade-limited loading.

lambda_gm_single_site_loading_rate_s_inv.description: The one-atom loading rate per available nanofiber trap site inferred from the initial ΛGM loading slope.

lambda_gm_single_site_loading_rate_uncer.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the ΛGM one-atom loading rate.

rpgc_single_site_loading_rate_s_inv.description: The one-atom loading rate per available nanofiber trap site inferred from the initial RPGC loading slope.

rpgc_single_site_loading_rate_uncertaint.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the RPGC one-atom loading rate.

lambda_gm_one_atom_loss_rate_s_inv.description: The one-atom loss rate for trapped atoms under the ΛGM cooling condition.

lambda_gm_one_atom_loss_rate_uncertainty.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the ΛGM one-atom loss rate.

rpgc_one_atom_loss_rate_s_inv.description: The one-atom loss rate for trapped atoms under the RPGC cooling condition.

rpgc_one_atom_loss_rate_uncertainty_s_in.description: The one-standard-error uncertainty of the RPGC one-atom loss rate.

normalized_two_body_loss_rate_s_inv.description: The normalized two-body loss rate κ/(4V) for the specified nanofiber trap volume and Cs two-body loss coefficient.

lambda_gm_loading_regime.description: The rate-equation loading regime inferred for ΛGM from the measured loading and loss rates relative to the collisional blockade criterion.

rpgc_loading_regime.description: The rate-equation loading regime inferred for RPGC from the measured loading and loss rates relative to the collisional blockade criterion.
